title: Finite-cover locality of bounded constructibility and a fixed Tor interval
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^r U_i$ be a finite open covering, with open immersions $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; $r=0$ is allowed if $X$ is empty. Use the small pro-etale sites, constant coefficient ring sheaves, and derived categories of module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and let $a\leq b$ be integers. Write $K_i=K|_{U_i}$ for derived restriction. Write $\mathcal H^t$ for cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Assume that for each $i$ only finitely many $\mathcal H^t(K_i)$ are nonzero, and each $\mathcal H^t(K_i)$ has a finite partition of $U_i$ into locally closed constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] subschemes (with their reduced induced structure) on which its pullback is locally constant [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf] with finite $A$-module stalks. Assume also that for every degree-zero sheaf $F_i$ of $A$-modules on $(U_i)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ one has
$$\mathcal H^t(K_i\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F_i)=0\quad(t\notin[a,b]),$$
using derived sheaf tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Then each $\mathcal H^t(K)$ has a finite partition of $X$ into locally closed constructible subschemes on which it is locally constant with finite $A$-module stalks, and for every degree-zero sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ one has
$$\mathcal H^t(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}F)=0\quad(t\notin[a,b]).$$
In particular $\mathcal H^t(K)=0$ for $t\notin[a,b]$, so $K$ is bounded constructible with Tor amplitude in that same interval.

proof.text: Use the equivalence from intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves to sheaves of modules over ULift A and its comparison with scheme pullback. Each open immersion into the Noetherian X is quasi-compact. Apply the existing fixed-module jointly-surjective quasi-compact pullback detection theorem to the identity of the encoded sheaf. If every local pullback is zero its identity is zero, so the encoded sheaf and then the original sheaf are zero. This includes an empty cover of an empty scheme. The Lean implementation uses ProEtale.eq_zero_of_forall_upperStar_map_eq_zero in the adopted source library.

proof.text: Exact constant-ring pullback commutes with derived homology. Therefore every globally nonzero homology degree belongs to the union, over the finite cover, of the local nonzero-degree sets. The latter union is finite by the local boundedness hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 095F, boundedness on a finite cover

proof.text: For each local finite stratification T_a, form g_ab:T_ab -> U_a -> X and the closed subscheme C_a defined by the vanishing ideal of the complement of the union of earlier opens U_b, b<a. Take the strata T_ab times_X C_a with their composed immersions into X. Their images are the local stratum images minus the earlier opens. These images are locally closed and hence constructible in the Noetherian X. They are pairwise disjoint: in different opens the later one excludes the earlier one, and in the same open the original strata are disjoint. They cover X by choosing the least open containing each point. The pullback projections give actual factorizations through the original local strata. This proves the needed refinement directly on the given finite open cover, without an affine refinement.

source.place: Tag 095F, finite global refinement; the construction of lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated

proof.text: Under the intrinsic/fixed-module constructibility equivalence, choose a stratification for every local restriction and use the preceding refinement. Finite local constancy pulls back along each factorization: base-change its trivializing pro-etale covering family, use pullback composition to compare the two restrictions in the cartesian square, and use preservation of constant module sheaves by inverse image. The same finite coefficient modules trivialize the pulled-back sheaf. Transport through the restriction-pullback comparison and the constructibility equivalence proves the global intrinsic constructibility assertion.

source.place: Tag 095F, pullback of the locally constant finite restrictions; constant-sheaf inverse-image adjunction

proof.text: Construct a pro-etale tensor model from the native derived-monoidal localization and its natural K-flat representative isomorphism. Apply this isomorphism to the exact K-flat resolution chosen in the intrinsic tensor definition and the chosen representative of the other argument; the resolution quasi-isomorphism identifies the native tensor of the representatives with that of the given derived objects. The canonical pro-etale tensor-pullback comparison for this model and exact pullback of single complexes give pullback(K tensor^L F) isomorphic to pullback(K) tensor^L single(pullback(F)). For every degree outside [a,b], local Tor vanishing makes the homology of every local pullback zero. The homology comparison and the zero-detection argument of step 1 give the global Tor assertion.
